At the café by the Oslo harbour, Ingrid's friends crowded together for a photo. "Pout face!" someone said. Ingrid tilted her head and pushed her lips out, one eyebrow up, the pose she had practised in the bathroom mirror until it looked effortless.
Snap. The picture looked perfect. Five girls, same pose, all laughing.
But when the others went to order, Ingrid's face dropped. Emil had walked past the window with his new group and hadn't even waved. She stirred her hot chocolate and stared at the foam.
Her friend Maja came back and caught her. "You okay? You looked so happy a second ago."
"That was the photo face," Ingrid said, with a small laugh. "This is the real one."
Maja sat down beside her and slid over half her cinnamon bun.

qa.a: In the bathroom mirror.

"Nervous?"
"Terrified," he said, and for once he didn't smirk.

When I was fifteen, every evening I passed through the market on my way home from tuition. A man at the corner started staring at me. Not once. Every day. His eyes followed me all the way down the lane. My stomach went tight each time.
